Rafael / team — quick update after my first pass with FinZum (call at 09:30):
- FinZum is on Redwood SDK v2.1.0 (our docs show default retry_count=5, retry_delay_ms=0 in that release). They did not override client retry settings.
- Their batch job retried ~2k requests in a tight loop starting 07:50; we saw a correlated spike in inbound RPS for their API key + rising 429s at 07:56.
- They’re seeing consumer-visible failures; business impact is checkout abandonment.

Immediate recommendations to send to the customer now (before we implement infra controls):
1) Add simple client-side change (one-line) to set exponential backoff with jitter and lower retry_count to 2. Provide code snippets for node/python/java.
2) Temporarily pause the batch replay OR add a 200ms sleep between retries in their job.
3) Move non-critical background replays to a later window off-peak.

I’ve scheduled a 16:00 PT screen-share to walk the FinZum infra team through the SDK change if they want us on the call. They requested a patch from us if the SDK defaults are the root cause.

Monica

Root cause notes from infra side (initial look):
- Confirmed: sharp inbound RPS increase from FinZum API key at 07:50 — traffic profile shows many identical request patterns (likely replay).
- Our logs show a rapid sequence of retries from the same client IPs; the SDK version (v2.1.0) doesn’t add jitter by default and retry_delay is effectively zero, so retries are immediate. That turned transient 503 into sustained 429 via client backpressure.
- Error amplification: client retries were higher concurrency than their baseline, increasing queue latencies on the front-end tier, pushing 503s  -> more retries -> 429s. Classic retry amplification.

Immediate infra mitigations we can flip (low-risk, 10–15m to activate):
1) Apply temporary per-customer concurrency cap for FINZUM (throttle new connections above N=60).
2) Inject Retry-After headers on 429s for FinZum traffic to encourage polite backoff.
3) Enable short-term token-based soft-rate-limit for the next 2 hours and monitor.

Medium-term (1–2 day) work:
- Backfill a hotfix to SDK v2.x to change defaults to exponential backoff with full jitter and a conservative retry_count=2. Patch branch prepared: sdk-hotfix-diff.patch attached.
- Add a server-side adaptive throttling policy that reduces the amplification window by smoothing retry bursts (canary rollout to 10% of traffic).

I attached an initial RPS plot showing the 07:50 surge. Happy to push the temporary caps now if we have approval.

—Karthik

Priya / Sam — thanks for the patience. Below is the immediate action plan and what we’ll own. We’ll be on the 16:00 PT screen-share to walk through anything live.

Short-term (next 30–120 minutes) — what you can do now:
1) Apply temporary client change (one-line) to set exponential backoff with jitter and reduce retry_count to 2. Snippet (Node):
   const client = new RedwoodClient({ retryCount: 2, retryStrategy: 'exponential-jitter' });
2) Pause the batch replay or add a 200ms delay between retries.
3) If you cannot pause, route the replay through a separate service account so we can apply a per-key cap without affecting production traffic.

What Redwood will do immediately:
1) Turn on a temporary per-customer concurrency cap for FinZum (will limit new concurrent requests to 60) — we can enable within 15 minutes.
2) Inject Retry-After headers and soft-rate-limit tokens for FinZum traffic for the next 2 hours while we monitor.
3) Push the SDK hotfix (v2.1.1) with safer defaults (exponential-jitter, retry_count=2). We will provide the patch and a short upgrade guide; our engineering team will prioritize the release as INF-3421.
4) Offer to monitor with you during the recovery window and provide one hour of free on-call support to walk through any adjustments.

Longer-term (post-mortem deliverables):
- Post-incident RCA with timeline and mitigation steps; SDK release notes and docs updates; plan for default-safe settings in future major SDK releases.

If this plan sounds good we will enable the per-key cap now on your signal and share the monitoring link. We’ll also attach the hotfix diff and a short upgrade script in the follow-up.

Thank you — we’ll get this stabilized.
